receiver.message_back: Thank you for your revised draft. We require (i) explicit mutuality throughout the release and confidentiality provisions, (ii) a carve-out permitting disclosures to regulators/rightful authorities (not only as strictly required by law), (iii) clarification that the non-disparagement obligation is mutual and time-limited (e.g., two years), and (iv) confirmation that this settlement resolves all regulatory exposures arising from the subject matter to the fullest extent permitted by law. Please revert with your client's position on these points.

drafter.private_reasoning: We should (i) accept mutuality in the release, confidentiality, and non-disparagement, as this is standard and provides reciprocal protection. (ii) For the carve-out, we can broaden disclosures to regulators or authorities beyond "required by law"—this is reasonable and pre-empts trouble if a regulator inquires. (iii) For non-disparagement, accept mutuality and propose a two-year term as suggested. (iv) For full resolution of regulatory exposures, we need to be careful due to the pending Tenbrook issue; we can agree to include language resolving regulatory exposures "to the fullest extent permitted by law," but avoid waiving obligations to cooperate with regulatory bodies or to make disclosures if later compelled. This preserves our position without tipping off the other side to Tenbrook specifically.

4. A clarification in the release that this settlement resolves all regulatory exposures arising from the subject matter, to the fullest extent permitted by law.

Please let us know if you require any further changes or clarifications.

Kind regards,
Aldous Finch LLP
